newsitem.title: CHINA: China raises more business taxes in February.
newsitem.headline: China raises more business taxes in February.

text.p: China's industrial and commercial tax revenues in February were 40.521 billion yuan ($4.88 billion), up 16.5 percent or 5.73 billion yuan from the same month in 1996, the Legal Daily said on Friday.

Value-added and consumption tax, making up more than half of total industrial and commercial tax collection, rose by 16.3 percent or 3.265 billion yuan from February 1996, the newspaper said, quoting the State Administration of Taxation.
Revenues from sales tax grew by 11.2 percent compared with the same month of last year while revenues from individual income tax rose by 38.9 percent, it said.
Industrial and commercial tax receipts in the first two months jumped 14.7 percent compared with the same period of last year, it said.
However, growing defaults in tax payments by enterprises were hampering collection, the newspaper said.
By the end of February, about 35.641 billion yuan of taxes remained unpaid by enterprises, an increase of 11.4 billion yuan compared with the same period of last year, it said.
